description: NEW regression introduced by the FIND-013 fix. healthcheck-lib.sh:24-30 adds a 10-minute stale-lock steal path: `if ! mkdir "$LOCK_DIR"; then lage=...; if [ "$lage" -ge 10 ]; then rmdir "$LOCK_DIR"||true; mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" || return 0; ...`. The staleness check (stat) and the steal (rmdir+mkdir) are NOT atomic together: if two invocations of the SAME loop's healthcheck are alive at the same time (plausible after a macOS sleep/wake catch-up burst, or if a prior run hung), both can independently observe lage>=10, both call rmdir (idempotent no-op on the second), then both call mkdir -- the first mkdir succeeds and creates a fresh lock, the second process's rmdir (which does not re-check staleness) deletes that fresh lock, and the second process's mkdir then also succeeds. Both processes now believe they hold the exclusive lock and run the full hc_run body concurrently (double DEAD/STUCK/STALE checks, double _restart pkill/bash --restart calls, potential double _selffix spawn attempts). Mitigated somewhat by ThrottleInterval=60 in the healthcheck plists (capafy-loop/launchd/ai.anicca.capafy-loop-healthcheck.plist:6) which makes exact-timing overlap less likely under normal conditions, but the race is real and specifically reachable in the exact abnormal-kill scenario the FIND-013 fix was designed to recover from -- i.e. the fix for the 'permanent lock' bug reintroduces a 'double-run' bug in the same narrow window.

evidence.snippet:
if ! mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
  local lage=...
  if [ "$lage" -ge 10 ]; then rmdir "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null||true; mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || return 0
  ...  else return 0; fi
fi
